column3: The Hebrew calls the proposed building a house; BSB specifies a palace.
The Hebrew describes David’s kingdom as raised high with a passive form; BSB makes the LORD the active subject exalting it.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name before his fathering more children; BSB leaves the second subject implicit.
The Hebrew repeats David after his anointing and again as the object of the search; BSB uses pronouns.
The Hebrew repeats go up in the LORD’s answer; BSB says Go without the upward direction.
The Hebrew leaves those going up unnamed and then names David twice; BSB supplies David and his men first and uses pronouns afterward.
The Hebrew leaves the people abandoning the gods unnamed and separately says they were burned; BSB names the Philistines and describes David ordering that the gods be burned.
The Hebrew says to come against them opposite the trees; BSB explicitly calls this attacking them.
The Hebrew directly says God has gone out before David; BSB adds that the marching sound will mean this.
The Hebrew calls the Philistine force a camp; BSB uses army.
The Hebrew speaks of David’s name going out and the LORD putting his dread upon the nations; BSB uses fame and causing the nations to fear him.
